image_description: An underwater shot of a hammerhead shark swimming diagonally from bottom-left to top-right. The shark has a distinct T-shaped head (cephalofoil), grey dorsal side, and lighter ventral side. It is surrounded by blue water with a rocky, textured background and several smaller, blurry fish in the distance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the laterally expanded, dorsoventrally flattened cephalofoil (hammer-shaped head).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The T-shaped head structure is clearly visible and dominates the anterior profile of the subject.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned at the extreme lateral tips of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Dark spots consistent with eyes are visible at the very ends of the hammer structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned near the lateral margins of the cephalofoil.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Resolution and lighting conditions prevent clear visualization of nostrils; they are too small to verify definitively.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Anterior margin of the cephalofoil is straight to slightly curved with a central indentation in some species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The leading edge of the head appears relatively straight with a subtle central curve, matching typical hammerhead morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is streamlined and laterally compressed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body tapers smoothly towards the tail and exhibits the characteristic thin profile of a shark when viewed from above/side.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal coloration is grey to brownish with white ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The top of the shark is grey, transitioning to a lighter/white underside, consistent with countershading.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A prominent, triangular dorsal fin is visible on the back, positioned correctly relative to the pectoral fins.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pectoral fins are broad and triangular.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Caudal fin is asymmetrical with a pronounced upper lobe.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail fin shows the classic heterocercal shape with a larger upper lobe compared to the lower lobe.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin appears overly smooth and plastic-like, lacking the expected micro-texture or specular highlights associated with wet, rough shark skin. This is common in AI generations but visually noticeable upon close inspection.
The background elements exhibit a 'smudged' or painterly blur rather than optical depth-of-field blur. Some background fish shapes appear slightly melted into the rock texture.
